purpose: Higher-powered public-data confirmation of the episode-multiplicity and onset-versus-persistence mechanisms identified in IRIS_EPISODE_NORMALIZED_CAUSAL_BENCHMARK_V1. This is external/public confirmation and does not access the protected post-2025 local cohort.
primary_questions: How many nominal 24-hour positive windows correspond to distinct physical >=10 MeV, >=10 pfu SEP episodes?
How many positive windows are already-active persistence cases versus genuine new-onset cases?
How much total positive statistical mass is removed when every physical SEP episode receives total weight 1?
Does the public stored target agree with an independent event-interval reconstruction of the stated next-24-hour operational threshold target?

frozen_semantics.issue_time: start of the 24-hour prediction window derived from the published predictor/prediction-window timestamp fields; if that mapping is ambiguous, stop before scoring
frozen_semantics.forecast_interval: (issue_time, issue_time + 24h] for new onset; overlap diagnostics additionally report any intersection with [issue_time, issue_time + 24h]
frozen_semantics.physical_episode: one catalogued operational >10 MeV episode with threshold >=10 pfu, using published start/end fields without merging distinct catalog rows post hoc
frozen_semantics.persistence: issue_time lies inside a physical operational threshold episode
frozen_semantics.new_onset: issue_time is not already inside an episode and an episode start occurs in (issue_time, issue_time + 24h]
frozen_semantics.episode_normalization: for uniquely mapped positive windows, each physical episode receives total positive weight exactly 1 split equally across its mapped positive windows
frozen_semantics.ambiguous_mapping: a window mapping to more than one physical episode is reported separately and excluded from episode-level inferential weighting; it is not silently assigned
frozen_semantics.unresolved: missing or contradictory required timestamps/episode bounds are unresolved rather than imputed

primary_outputs: total windows and stored target counts
episode multiplicity factor = uniquely mapped positive windows / represented episodes
distribution of windows per physical episode
episode-normalized positive mass versus ordinary positive-window mass
source file hashes and exact upstream commit

predeclared_interpretation.strong_confirmation: Episode multiplicity factor >=1.5 AND persistence windows exceed new-onset windows, with both effects directly reproducible from public timestamps.
predeclared_interpretation.partial_confirmation: Either episode multiplicity factor >1.0 or persistence constitutes a substantial positive-window fraction, but not both strong-confirmation conditions.
predeclared_interpretation.null_or_refutation: Episode multiplicity factor is approximately 1 and already-active persistence is rare relative to genuine onset; retain result without redefining episodes or windows.

secondary_model_analysis.authorization: Allowed only after the primary model-free audit is complete and only if the pinned repository exposes timestamp-aligned prediction probabilities or a clearly leakage-safe feature table whose future-target/event metadata columns can be excluded deterministically.
preferred_models_if_refit_is_needed: current-proton-active persistence diagnostic if issue-time proton state is directly available
elastic-net logistic regression with the already-frozen IRIS benchmark settings
five-seed-median XGBoost with the already-frozen IRIS benchmark settings
secondary_model_analysis.rule: If safe timestamp/prediction alignment or leakage-safe feature definition cannot be established from the pinned public source, do not improvise; report model analysis as not admissible.
